issues.description: Identifier naming inconsistency: the exercise and helpers refer to a function named simulate_msd_one_round, but the template defines simulate_one_round. Specifically, the problem statement and plot_msd helper call simulate_msd_one_round, while the template file defines def simulate_one_round(...). The solution repository implements simulate_msd_one_round. This mismatch will cause NameError/ImportError and prevents running the provided plotting/testing code and tests that expect simulate_msd_one_round.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the identifier consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: rename the template function simulate_one_round to simulate_msd_one_round (update its def line and any internal references) so it matches the problem statement, plot_msd helper, and tests. Alternatively, update plot_msd and the problem statement to call simulate_one_round, but ensure tests and solution remain consistent.

issues.description: Concept: the single-round MSD simulation function. The problem statement (and the solution implementation) refer to this function as simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) -> tuple[float, float]. The template repository instead provides a stub named simulate_one_round(n_shots: int, p: float) -> tuple[float, float] and leaves simulate_msd_one_round undefined (meanwhile plot_msd in the template calls simulate_msd_one_round). This naming mismatch prevents a direct mapping from the task description to the starter code, and causes runtime/name errors when students run plot_msd or follow the instructions. Students will be blocked or forced to rename functions or add aliases to make the code run.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the identifier across artifacts. Rename the template stub simulate_one_round(...) to simulate_msd_one_round(...), or add a one-line alias in the template: def simulate_msd_one_round(n_shots, p): return simulate_one_round(n_shots, p). Also ensure any internal callers (e.g., plot_msd) call the same simulate_msd_one_round identifier so the problem statement, template, and solution consistently use the same function name.
